newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares bounce back after Wednesday's slide.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares bounce back after Wednesday's slide.

text.p: Danish share prices rose on Thursday, recouping much of the losses caused by Wednesday's profit-taking and looking set to continue upward on Friday.
"Market sentiment continues to be positive and there seems to be no reason not to end the week positively," a dealer said.
He added that as in recent days banking and finance shares propelled the market on Thursday.

The KFX top-20 index gained 0.63 point to 121.56 in overall bourse turnover of 834 million crowns. The KFX September future rose 0.30 point to 121.40 with 90 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Unidanmark was the day's most traded share, rising three crowns to 273 crowns in turnover of 282,578 trades.
Den Danske Bank closed four crowns up, at 428 crowns and BG Bank rose two crowns to 224.

Analysts have been saying for some time that Danish bank shares are seen as somewhat undervalued compared to those of foreign finance houses and investors are keen to increase their weighting in their portfolios.
Contrary to expectations A.P. Moeller shares were unmoved by reports that it planned to become more open with information. --Claus Mathisen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969652
